claims.text: A 50–100 nm TiN layer should be deposited between the zirconium-alloy substrate and the elemental Cr coating.
The 50–100 nm TiN interlayer will hinder elevated-temperature Cr–Zr interdiffusion.
The TiN interlayer will preserve Cr-coating protection in subcritical water at approximately 300°C.
The TiN interlayer will preserve Cr-coating protection during steam exposure at approximately 1200°C for 5–10 minutes.
PVD techniques can be used to introduce the proposed interfacial layer on a zirconium-alloy substrate.
A graded interface or surface treatment can address adhesion and thermal-expansion mismatch in the TiN/Cr/Zr system.
Approximately 300°C subcritical-water exposure represents normal reactor operation for this test.
Steam exposure at approximately 1200°C for 5–10 minutes represents accident-relevant conditions.
The deposited TiN layer will be continuous, dense, and physically isolate the Cr coating from the zirconium-alloy substrate.
TiN has very low atomic diffusivity.
The TiN layer will greatly inhibit atomic exchange between Cr and Zr at elevated temperature.
Suppressing interdiffusion and intermetallic formation will preserve coating microstructure and adhesion.
TiN will remain chemically stable in both approximately 300°C subcritical water and approximately 1200°C steam.
Relative to an elemental Cr coating without an interfacial barrier, the TiN-interfaced coating will show markedly less Cr–Zr interdiffusion.
Relative to the baseline, the TiN-interfaced coating will have improved structural integrity under accident conditions.
Relative to the baseline, the TiN-interfaced coating will have improved corrosion resistance under accident conditions.
The TiN-interfaced coating will retain effective protection during prolonged subcritical-water exposure.
